hints: Look at this in two separate parts, first compare how much nitrogen each formula contains for its mass, then think about acidity.
Calculate $M_r$ for each salt and find mass of N in one mole, $\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3$ has $M_r = 80$ with 28 g of N, while $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4$ has $M_r = 132$ with 28 g of N.
Remember the $\text{NH}_4^+$ ion acts as a weak acid in water to release $\text{H}^+$, so decide if that will raise or lower soil pH.
walkthrough:
**Compare percentage of nitrogen by mass**

Think of percentage as mass of nitrogen in one mole divided by the molar mass. Both salts contain 2 N atoms per formula unit, so the lighter salt has the higher percentage.

$$M_r(\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3) = 14 + 4 + 14 + 48 = 80$$
$$M_r((\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4) = 28 + 8 + 32 + 64 = 132$$

**Calculate the percentages**

Each mole contains $2 \times 14 = 28$ g of N. Divide by $M_r$ and multiply by 100.

$$\%N \text{ in } \text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3 = \frac{28}{80} \times 100 = 35.0\%$$
$$\%N \text{ in } (\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4 = \frac{28}{132} \times 100 = 21.2\%$$
So ammonium nitrate has the higher percentage of nitrogen by mass.

**Decide the effect on soil pH**

Both salts contain the ammonium ion, $\text{NH}_4^+$, which is the conjugate acid of a weak base. In wet soil it hydrolyses to release $\text{H}^+$.

$$\text{NH}_4^+(aq) \rightleftharpoons \text{NH}_3(aq) + \text{H}^+(aq)$$
More $\text{H}^+$ means more acidic, so pH decreases. The anions $\text{NO}_3^-$ and $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ come from strong acids and do not hydrolyse to affect pH.

**Combine both conclusions**

Higher nitrogen is ammonium nitrate, and effect is decrease in pH. That matches the row with ammonium nitrate and decrease.

options.A: Correct. Ammonium nitrate ($M_r$ 80) is lighter than ammonium sulfate ($M_r$ 132) but both contain 28 g N per mole, so nitrate is about 35% N compared to about 21% N. Both release H+ by hydrolysis of NH4+, so wet neutral soil becomes acidic and pH decreases.
options.B: Incorrect on pH. It correctly identifies ammonium nitrate as higher in N, but NH4+ is acidic, not basic. Students choosing this may think ammonia or nitrate makes soil alkaline, forgetting the hydrolysis equilibrium NH4+ to NH3 + H+.
options.C: Incorrect on percentage. It correctly says pH decreases, but picks ammonium sulfate as higher in N. This is the trap of seeing two NH4 groups in the formula and assuming more nitrogen, without dividing by the much larger Mr of 132 due to sulfate.
options.D: Incorrect on both parts. Ammonium sulfate has the lower %N, and NH4+ salts lower pH rather than raise it. Students may confuse sulfate with basic behaviour or miscalculate Mr.
